drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A marketing coordinator at a company on a Team plan
drills.answer_line: SAM: Right. The answer is B.
drills.stem: On a Team plan, a marketing coordinator wants her campaign Project to use brand guidelines and briefs kept in the company's Google Drive. The Google Drive connector is not available to her. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Download the files each week and upload them to the Project by hand
options.B: Ask the Owner or Primary Owner to enable the Google Workspace connectors for the organisation
options.C: Connect her Drive through a personal Claude account instead
options.D: Paste the Drive folder's link into the chat and ask Claude to open it

drills.why: On Team and Enterprise, an Owner or Primary Owner enables the connectors at org level. A is a weekly chore with stale snapshots; C leaves the org's controls; D has no connection.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A sales lead sets up a shared Project
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. It is a rule for how Claude behaves in every chat in this Project
drills.stem: A sales lead sets up a shared Project for her team's proposals. Every proposal must follow a five-section structure and use British spelling. Where should that requirement go?

options.A: In her own profile settings, so Claude always writes that way for her
options.B: In the Project's instructions, so it applies to every chat in the Project
options.C: In a note at the top of each proposal chat
options.D: In an uploaded "style notes" document, with no instructions pointing to it

drills.why: A behaviour rule for every chat and every user of the Project is a project instruction. Profile settings reach only her; notes rely on memory; D is reference, not a rule.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. An HR partner's policy Project
drills.answer_line: SAM: Half right. A is in.
drills.stem: Choose two. An HR policy Project keeps quoting old parental leave terms. The handbook was updated in Google Drive two weeks ago; the knowledge holds a PDF exported last spring. Which two actions fix this?

options.A: Add the handbook from Google Drive, so the linked Google Doc keeps syncing
options.B: Remove the old PDF from the Project's knowledge
options.D: Add an instruction saying "always use the latest policy"
options.E: Turn on research for policy questions

drills.why: One current, syncing source and nothing stale beside it. D is a polite instruction with the old copy still retrievable; C is the bigger-model reflex; E searches the web.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A consultant's Project instructions read
drills.answer_line: SAM: Good instinct to check, but here the length is doing work.
drills.stem: A consultant's Project instructions read "You are helpful. Be accurate." Outputs vary in format and sometimes cite an old engagement letter still in the knowledge. What is the best fix?

options.A: Rewrite "be accurate" in capitals and add "never make mistakes"
options.B: State role, audience, format and authoritative sources, add a fallback rule, and remove the old letter
options.C: Paste the text of every knowledge file into the instructions
options.D: Start each chat in research mode

drills.why: A stated format fixes the drift; naming the authority and removing the stale letter fixes the citation. A is louder guidance; C bloats and keeps the stale file; D searches the web.

drills.label: Dropdown
drills.question_line: SAM: One more, in the dropdown style. Pause here and answer before we go on.
drills.answer_line: SAM: All four. One never changes
drills.prompt: For each, choose upload, connect, or hold and check policy. 1: a signed master services agreement that will not change. 2: a weekly pricing sheet in Google Drive. 3: this week's client emails, to summarise actions. 4: an HR export with home addresses and salaries, where policy restricts personal data.
drills.answer: 1 upload. 2 connect via Google Drive. 3 connect Gmail. 4 hold and check policy; remove or anonymise personal details first.

drills.question_line: SAM: Recall first. Pause and name the four segments, and the question that ran under all of them.
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Instructions and knowledge, uploads and connectors
drills.prompt: Name the four segments, and the question that ran under all of them.
drills.answer: Instructions and knowledge; uploads and connectors; instructions that work; keeping it current. Where does each piece belong, and who keeps it current?

In this episode: Split a Project into instructions and knowledge
Choose upload or connector: Google Drive, Gmail
Cold open: the missing connector: Team plan, brand files in Google Drive
Connector not available to her; launch is Friday
Four objectives: configure, manage sources, instructions, maintain
Underneath: where does each piece belong, and who keeps it current?
Segment one: instructions and knowledge: Instructions: how Claude behaves in every chat in the Project
Knowledge: documents, text and code used across the Project's chats
Profile settings apply to all your conversations; project instructions to one Project
Paid plans: retrieval near the context limit, up to 10x capacity
Curate: one current version, nothing superseded
Keep instructions concise; limit active tools and connectors
Segment two: uploads and connectors: Upload holds the version you uploaded
Linked Google Doc keeps syncing with Drive
Drive: Sheets, Slides, PDFs, Office; embedded images not processed
Claude opens only what your Google account can access
Gmail: search, read, draft; attachment details, not content
Scope connectors to the Project's job
Segment three: instructions that work: "Be helpful, be accurate" gives Claude nothing to act on
Role and audience; task and format
Which knowledge is authoritative, and for what
Fallback: say so when knowledge does not cover it
Behaviour rules in instructions; reference material in knowledge
Segment four: keeping it current: Update knowledge and instructions when a source changes
Retest with standard questions after a change
Cold open: the verdict: Weekly manual uploads: snapshots that go stale
Org-level connectors are enabled by the Owner or Primary Owner
A personal account sits outside the organisation's controls
A pasted link is not a connection
Tell: "not available to her" on Team or Enterprise
Five to remember: Instructions = behaviour; knowledge = what it knows; profile = only you
Retrieval expands capacity; curate to one current version
Upload what never changes; connect what does
Role, audience, format, authority, fallback; manuals in knowledge
Owner, update on change, retest, edit access for maintainers
Recap: the exam tells: Rule for every chat in a shared Project → project instructions
One person's preference everywhere → profile settings
Quotes an old version → link the live source, remove the stale file
Changes weekly → connect; never changes → upload
Connector missing on a Team plan → Owner or Primary Owner
"Be helpful, be accurate" → role, format, authority, fallback
Manual pasted into instructions → move it to knowledge
Shared Project keeps drifting → owner, edit access, retest
